Actual gross expenditure increased from £40.01m (2023/24) to £48.1m (2024/25). The auditor flagged this as consistent with cost pressures not fully controlled.
findings.matters: This rate of cost growth (24% in one year, driven partly by revaluations and technical items) is a warning signal. Even though the council achieved a £1m surplus against budget, the underlying cost base is expanding faster than the financial strategy assumes.
findings.figures: Total net service spend per head: lowest in 18/19, now above national mean; gross expenditure £40.01m (2023/24) to £48.1m (2024/25)
findings.quote: Total net service spend per head: The Council had the lowest spend per head in 18/19, but this has increased year-on-year. The Council has increased much faster than the mean which appears to be relatively stable. This has increased further to £48.1m in 2024/25.

findings.headline: Strategic budget-balancing risk scored 16 (high) with no active mitigation strategy; council is tolerating the risk
findings.detail: Risk BBC05 relates to long-term balancing of the budget and related constraints. It has been scored at 16 (high risk) and has remained unchanged from 2023/24. The auditor noted the council is tolerating the risk and taking no additional action beyond existing controls (medium-term budgetary process, sound level of services, efficiency plans).
findings.matters: A high-rated strategic risk being tolerated with no active mitigation, combined with £1.4–1.8m annual savings targets and a departing finance officer, suggests the council has limited confidence in its ability to actively close medium-term funding gaps beyond hoped-for efficiency delivery.
findings.figures: Risk score 16 (high); unchanged since 2023/24
findings.quote: The strategic risk 'BBC05' on the quarter two risk report, is scored at 16 (high risk). This has remained unchanged from 2023/24. The risk report states the Council is tolerating the risk, and therefore no additional action is to be taken.

findings.headline: Section 151 Officer departed March 2025, creating knowledge loss risk on budget and efficiency planning
findings.detail: The outgoing S151 officer was heavily involved in efficiency programme discussions and budget planning, but processes have not been formally documented. With that person now gone, the auditor flagged that 'if processes, actions and priorities are not formally documented, there is a risk to the Council that key knowledge will be lost. This will hinder the Council's ability to continue to effectively make savings.'
findings.matters: Continuity and institutional knowledge are critical during a period of high savings targets and restructuring. An unplanned departure of the S151 officer compounds the governance weakness in the efficiency programme and could delay or derail the £1.4–1.8m annual savings.
findings.figures: S151 departure March 2025
findings.quote: The outgoing S151 officer was heavily involved in the discussion and updating of the long list and has left the organisation in March 2025. Therefore, if processes, actions and priorities are not formally documented, there is a risk to the Council that key knowledge will be lost.

findings.headline: Internal Drainage Board levy is a structural cost pressure, growing at 40% annually and forecasted to rise from £2.8m to £3.2m by 2028/29
findings.detail: The IDB levy has increased on average 40% year-on-year from 2021/22 and is now the largest controllable cost pressure facing the council. The auditor noted that increases have been built into the five-year financial strategy and the council is lobbying government. Boston received £431k of exceptional government funding for 2024-25 to offset this.
findings.matters: A 40% average levy increase annually is unsustainable and absorbs savings that should otherwise improve financial resilience. Future government support cannot be assumed. This is a structural cost pressure specific to Boston's geography and drainage liability.
findings.figures: £2.8m budgeted 2024-25; forecasted £3.2m by 2028/29; 40% average increases from 2021/22; £431k exceptional government support 2024-25
findings.quote: Internal Drainage Board (IDB) levy continues to be a cost pressure for the Council with a budgeted cost of £2.8m in 2024-25. The Council have seen increases on average of 40% of the levy from 2021/22. Forecasted increases have been built into the five-year financial strategy budgeted to increase to £3.2m in 2028/29.

findings.headline: Efficiency savings programme lacks formal governance, at risk from departing S151 officer
findings.detail: The auditor found no formal programme in place to effectively identify, RAG-rate and monitor efficiencies. The efficiency list has no due dates, key meetings are unminuted, and the outgoing S151 officer (who left March 2025) was heavily involved in updating priorities. Internal audit found insufficient controls to test. This is a repeated finding from prior year, with management's due date to fix it now 30 September 2025.
findings.matters: The council needs £1.4–1.8m in annual savings for the next five years. Without documented processes and with key knowledge walking out the door, there is execution risk on the savings targets that underpin financial sustainability.
findings.figures: £1.4m required 2025-26; £1.3m required 2026-27 and 2027-28; £1.8m required 2028-29
findings.quote: The efficiency programme we have obtained is a long list of potential efficiencies to be explored which are allocated to lead officers. This has been used to identify and report efficiencies during 2024-25. There are no due dates on the efficiency list therefore it cannot be seen if savings are falling behind plan.

news_drafts.headline: Boston audit finds governance gaps amid budget pressure
news_drafts.lead: Boston's internal audit has found serious gaps in how the council manages financial risk. Five actions from a prior audit remain overdue, some by more than a year, while a critical audit of the council's savings programme has not been started halfway through the financial year. A review of the finance team's capacity and capability has been waiting for management to respond to its draft report since March. These governance failures matter because the council faces sustained high-risk pressure to balance its long-term budget with government funding falling and service costs rising, and no improvement is planned. The audit committee heard more positive news: treasury investments outperformed budget by £169,389 in Q1, and delays in spending on buildings and equipment have left the council with more cash available for investment.
